name: Kenemu
description: A star 39 parsecs away, 3.3 times the Sun's width, measured from its light.

radius.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 95168: radius 3.253 solar radii, implied by the fitted luminosity 30.207 solar luminosities (fractional uncertainty 0.044) and temperature

temperature.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 95168: effective temperature 7508 +/- 180 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.029)

distance.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 95168: distance 38.926 pc, the paper's parallax inverted (Gaia DR1's where it revised the star's, else the Hipparcos reduction of van Leeuwen 2007; section 2.3; fractional uncertainty 0.007), at which the luminosity and radius hold

limb.none: no mass is measured and no spectroscopic surface gravity is published with this radius: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770 assume the gravity of their fit (table column 15)

text.card: A star 39 parsecs away, 3.3 times the Sun's width, measured from its light.
text.introduction: Its brightness, measured band by band, gives 30 times the Sun's luminosity at 7,508 K, so 3.253 solar radii.
text.locator: Table 2, HIP 95168: D, Teff, L, Rad, Q

quotes.title: Rho1 Sagittarii
quotes.card: Rho1 Sagittarii, Latinized from ρ1 Sagittarii, formally named Kenemu, is a single, variable star in the southern constellation of Sagittarius.
quotes.introduction: It has a white hue and is visible to the naked eye with an apparent visual magnitude that fluctuates around 3.93.

radialVelocity.source: SIMBAD's radial velocity for Gaia DR3 4084474835781915392 (quality E), from 1953GCRV..C......0W; Gaia DR3 measures none
